title: EV batteries last longer than drivers feared
gist: A 500,000-test Aviloo study across 20 EV models found batteries retain a median 87-94 percent of original capacity after 150,000 km, well above warranty replacement thresholds, but with wide model-specific variance (Nissan Leaf ZE1 spreads up to 13.5 points) driven by climate and parking-charge habits, fueling a UK push for mandatory battery health certification.

insights.claim: Aviloo's study of more than 500,000 battery tests across 20 popular EV models conducted between 2022 and 2026 found median state of health (SoH) of 87 to 94 percent after 150,000 km of driving.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Durability data undercuts a key consumer objection to EV adoption and could support used-EV residual values and continued EV demand.
insights.locator: According to the latest study published by Aviloo

insights.claim: EV battery warranties typically only guarantee replacement if capacity falls below 70 percent after eight years or 100,000 miles (160,000 km), while the Aviloo study's median SoH of 87-94 percent at 150,000 km is well above that floor.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Real-world durability beating the warranty threshold by a wide margin suggests used-EV batteries may be undervalued relative to actual remaining life, an angle for used-EV pricing and financing models.
insights.locator: EV battery warranties typically cover eight years

insights.claim: Median SoH across the 20 tested models progressed from 91-97 percent at 50,000 km, to 88-95 percent at 100,000 km, to 87-94 percent at 150,000 km, showing degradation slows rather than accelerates with mileage.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: A decelerating degradation curve supports longer useful battery life than a linear extrapolation from early-mileage data would suggest, relevant to residual-value and total-cost-of-ownership modeling.
insights.locator: The median SoH was between 91 and 97 percent

themes.theme: Variance across models, climate, and habits

insights.claim: Battery degradation speed varies significantly even within the same EV model depending on climate conditions, battery size, and driver habits such as parking; the Aviloo study excluded Chinese EV models due to lack of data.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Model-level averages mask wide individual variance, so used-EV buyers and investors in resale markets should weight vehicle-specific battery-health certification over nameplate averages.
insights.locator: The Aviloo study, which did not include Chinese models

insights.claim: Nissan's Leaf ZE1 showed the widest SoH spread of the 20 models studied, up to 13.5 percentage points at 150,000 km, equivalent to about 29 km of real-world range per charge, attributed partly to its smaller battery requiring more frequent charging than other models.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Nissan's smaller-battery architecture may carry higher residual-value uncertainty than peers in the used-EV market, a specific model-level risk to flag.

insights.claim: Individual-vehicle SoH spreads reached up to 11 percentage points for Tesla's Model Y, 11 to 12 points for Volkswagen's ID.4, and more than 12 points for Hyundai's Ioniq 5, narrower than the Nissan Leaf but still meaningful.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Even leading-selling EV models show double-digit percentage-point variance in battery health at similar mileage, meaning nameplate SoH averages alone are insufficient for used-EV due diligence.
insights.locator: Aviloo said the spread between the individual cars

themes.theme: Charging and parking behavior drives degradation

insights.claim: Aviloo CEO Marcus Berger says batteries in hotter climates degrade faster, and that parking an EV at a high state of charge (80 to 100 percent) accelerates battery degradation; he recommends keeping parked charge between 30 and 70 percent, advice he says very few consumers know.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Consumer education gaps on charging habits represent a controllable variance driver relevant to automakers' and dealers' battery-health guidance and to warranty-cost modeling.
insights.quote: What very few consumers know is: don’t park your cars with 100, 90 or 80 percent state of charge. It’s just harming the battery
insights.locator: Berger said batteries of EVs in hotter climates

themes.theme: Used-EV market lacks a battery-health information standard

insights.claim: Unlike combustion vehicles, where age and mileage roughly track a car's condition, EV value assessment cannot rely on age and mileage alone because battery health depends heavily on how the vehicle was treated, a gap Aviloo's CEO says the used-car market does not yet price well.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: This information asymmetry is a market opportunity for battery-health data and certification services in used-EV pricing and financing.
insights.quote: The car might look the same—same age, same mileage—and you don’t know how it has been treated.
insights.locator: In contrast to a combustion engine car

insights.claim: Three of the UK's largest EV organizations recently called on the government to introduce mandatory battery health certifications, a push Tesla UK's used-car sales and delivery manager James Strong says would strengthen confidence and improve transparency in the used-EV market.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Mandatory battery-health certification, if adopted, would create a standardized data layer that could materially affect used-EV pricing and financing, a regulatory trend worth monitoring.
insights.quote: a nationally recognized battery state of health standards
insights.locator: Aviloo’s study came as three of the UK’s largest EV organizations
